header.running_head: Severing Ties with the Period of Ignorance to Strengthen Ties with Islaam

blocks.text:
when Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived with the captives from the Battle of Badr, they distributed them amongst the Sahabah (RA) saying, "I emphatically command you to treat them well." Amongst the prisoners was Abu Azeez bin Umayr bin Hishaam, the real brother of Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA). Hadhrat Abu Azeez (RA) says, "When I was captured by one of the Ansaar, my brother Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) passed by. He said to the Ansaari, 'Tie both his hands well because his mother is very wealthy and she will pay a large ransom for him.' I was with a group of Ansaar when we returned from the battle. Whenever the morning and afternoon meals were served, they gave me the bread and ate dates only because of the instruction of Rasulullaah ﷺ to treat us (prisoners) well. Whenever any of them happened to receive any bread, he would ensure that he gave it to me. When I returned it to him out of embarrassment, he would give it back without even touching it."
Hadhrat Abu Yasar (RA) was the Ansaari who captured Hadhrat Abu Azeez (RA). After Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) had told Hadhrat Abu Yasar (RA) what he did (about tying both hands well), Hadhrat Abu Azeez (RA) said, "Dear brother! Is this the advice you give him about me (your own brother)?" Hadhrat Mus'ab (RA) replied, "He (Hadhrat Abu Yasar (RA)) is my brother and not you." When Hadhrat Abu Azeez (RA)'s mother enquired what the highest ransom was that anyone from the Quraysh had paid, she was informed that it was four thousand Dirhams. She then sent four thousand Dirhams and ransomed her son.[^1]

Hadhrat Ayyoob bin Nu'maan narrates that during the Battle of Badr, Hadhrat Abu Azeez bin Umayr, the real brother of Hadhrat Mus'ab bin Umayr (RA) was also captured (by the Muslims). He was placed in the custody of Hadhrat Muhriz bin Nadhla (RA). Hadhrat Mus'ab (RA) said to Hadhrat Muhriz (RA), "Tie both his hands well because he has a very wealthy mother in Makkah (who will pay a large ransom for him)." Hadhrat Abu Azeez (RA) said, "Is that your advice concerning me, dear brother?" Hadhrat Mus'ab (RA) replied, "Muhriz is my brother and not you." Hadhrat Abu Azeez (RA)'s mother then sent four thousand Dirhams (as ransom for her son).[^2]
The Incident Between Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) and his Daughter Ummul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Ummu Habeebah (RA)

Hadhrat Zuhri reports that Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) once came to Madinah (before accepting Islaam) to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when Rasulullaah ﷺ had intended to go to war with the people of Makkah. Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) spoke to Rasulullaah ﷺ about extending the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (which the people of Makkah had already breached) but Rasulullaah ﷺ refused to do so.
